strings.name: Rafael Nadal
strings.summary: Born on Mallorca, Nadal entered professional tennis as a teenager and built his game around heavy left-handed topspin, movement and sustained competition. He retired in 2024 with 22 major singles titles, including 14 at Roland-Garros, and Olympic gold in singles and doubles. Repeated injuries interrupted a career that spanned more than two decades.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: Set a benchmark for clay-court competition through French Open and other major titles, with international influence on sporting culture.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Plays
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Fourteen Roland-Garros titles
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won the French Open singles title fourteen times from 2005 to 2022.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Success across surfaces and at the Olympics
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Won each of the four singles majors, plus Olympic singles gold in 2008 and doubles gold in 2016.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Life beyond the tour
strings.timeline.event-1.text: An ATP feature described his post-retirement focus on family, his academy and charitable foundation.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Retired after the Davis Cup
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Ended his professional career after representing Spain at the Davis Cup Finals in Malaga, with 22 major singles titles.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Australian Open and fourteenth French Open
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Won the Australian Open and a fourteenth French Open, taking his final major singles total to 22.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Olympic doubles gold in Rio
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Partnered Marc Lopez to win Olympic doubles gold, adding to his singles title from Beijing 2008.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Completed the career Grand Slam
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Won his first US Open to complete the set of four major singles titles.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Wimbledon, Olympic gold and No.1
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Won Wimbledon and Olympic singles gold in Beijing, then reached the ATP No.1 ranking for the first time.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: French Open title on debut
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won the French Open on his first main-draw appearance at nineteen, beginning his long dominance in Paris.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: First tour title
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Won his first ATP Tour singles title in Sopot, Poland, before his major breakthrough the following year.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Turned professional
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Turned professional and progressed through lower-level competition toward the ATP Tour.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born on Mallorca
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Manacor and introduced to tennis by his uncle Toni during childhood.
